result.title: Understanding Stability of Outer Nesterov Momentum on Stochastic Pseudo-Gradients
result.summary: Large neural networks are commonly trained across many workers, and communication between them is a major cost. Workers therefore take several local optimization steps before sending their net parameter displacements, or pseudo-gradients, to an outer optimizer, which often applies Nesterov momentum. We study how the outer momentum, the number of local steps and the averaging over workers control the training dynamics, and in particular their stability. For random quadratics, we derive an exact mean-square stability criterion in any dimension, which reveals that the inner batch size determines whether increasing the number of local steps eventually stabilizes or destabilizes the outer iteration. Moreover, while averaging the pseudo-gradients of independent workers can make larger outer momentum values admissible, the number of workers required for stability can grow exponentially with the number of local steps. Finally, we show that the mean-square dynamics governing stability can be probed directly at intermediate neural-network checkpoints using shared-minibatch perturbations. We test our theoretical findings across networks, and measure their consequences for training loss.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文研究分布式训练中「本地多步更新 + 外层 Nesterov 动量」的优化动力学，在随机二次函数上给出均方稳定性判据，并考察本地步数、内层批大小与 worker 平均对稳定性的影响，最后用共享小批扰动在检查点上探测该动力学。
